documents.title: Application for a Residential Service Agency License (Instructions, Section B 'Policies and Procedures' grid, and Required Attachment 3)
documents.form_number: None printed on the form. The file is APPLICATION_RSA-License-06.26.2026-A.pdf, 12 pages.
documents.issuer: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ)
documents.version: File dated 06.26.2026-A. It is the version linked from the OHCQ RSA page.
documents.how_used: This is the official OHCQ document for reviewing a new RSA's policies. Required Attachment 3 requires policies and procedures as specified in COMAR 10.07.05.08B. The 'Policies and Procedures' grid on pages 4-6 lists each required policy under five headings. For each item the applicant names the attached document and its page numbers, or enters N/A if a waiver is requested. The application form's own text is used for the item wording.

documents.title: COMAR 10.07.05.08 Administration (B. Policies and Procedures)
documents.issuer: Maryland Division of State Documents (Library of Maryland Regulations), for OHCQ/MDH
documents.version: Current online text as fetched; the page shows no effective date.
documents.how_used: This is the regulation behind the application grid. Its numbering, B(1)(a)(i) through B(1)(e)(v), supplies the item IDs, because the application grid has no numbers. COMAR 10.07.05.04A(2)(i) requires copies of these policies with the license application. COMAR 10.07.05.04I(3) requires renewal applicants to submit policies that have changed substantively.

required_items.text: Administration - Scope of services
required_items.cite: Application p.4 (Policies and Procedures > Administration); COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(a)(i)

required_items.text: Administration - Delineation of services provided by the agency when the agency coordinates care within the agency or with another provider
Administration - Notification to the client or client representative with legal authority to make health care decisions of the agency’s responsibilities to coordinate care when appropriate
Administration - Admission criteria
Administration - Assessment of potential clients before their acceptance into the program

Administration - Billing and service records, maintenance of charges, and similar items, except for those clients receiving services through a managed-care health benefits plan or third-party payor, in which case records are maintained as required by the third-party payor
Administration - Quality assurance program
Administration - Clinical management, including assessment, plans, delegation, and supervision
Personnel - Job descriptions and educational qualifications for all employees and contractors
Personnel - Skill assessments of all employees and contractors
Personnel - Health requirements for employees and contractors
Patient Care - Provision of home health care services and criteria for determining the need for skilled services
Patient Care - Administration of drugs
Patient Care - Enteral and parenteral nutrition procedures
Patient Care - Frequency of client monitoring
Patient Care - Training and retraining of clients or their family members, when indicated
Informed Consent - A client or client representative with legal authority to make legal decisions, signs an informed consent form consenting to changes to the agency’s recommended plan of care; or:
Informed Consent - A client signs an informed consent form consenting to assistance by a nonlicensed individual with treatments of a routine nature, or with the self-administration of medications
Environment and Safety - Preparation and storage of enteral formulas, intravenous therapies, other supplies, equipment, and similar items
Environment and Safety - Infection control procedures
Environment and Safety - Disposal of biomedical waste
Environment and Safety - Maintenance of equipment; and procedures
required_items.cite: Application p.6; COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(e)(iv). The application's wording is 'Maintenance of equipment; and procedures'. COMAR reads 'Maintenance of equipment'.

required_items.cite: Application p.6; COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(e)(v). COMAR's wording is 'Emergency procedures'.

notes: OHCQ publishes no separate policy checklist for RSAs. The policy requirements are the 'Policies and Procedures' grid in the RSA License Application (pp.4-6) and COMAR 10.07.05.08B, which the application cites. The application also requires a business plan (including a description of agency services), an organizational chart, an SDAT letter of good standing and workers' compensation proof. These are not policy content and are excluded here. How the reviewer expects submission: (1) Submit a typed application, with the policies and the other attachments, through the OHCQ 'Submit a License Application' link. The application says handwritten applications are returned, and that there is no application fee. (2) Submit the policies as attachments. In each grid box, list the name of the attached document and the page numbers where that policy appears. Organize the manual under the five headings above, in the same order. This makes it easy to cross-reference every B(1) item. (3) To request a waiver of any item, list the policy in the waiver box and explain why it is inappropriate or unnecessary for this RSA. Then enter N/A in that item's box. This follows COMAR 10.07.05.08B(2). (4) Agencies that provide invasive equipment or supplies must arrange 24-hour-a-day equipment maintenance service (COMAR 10.07.05.08B(3)). The application asks about this as a yes/no question. (5) The RSA Certification on worker classification of personal care aides is a separate online form under Health-General §19-4A-11. All applicants must complete it, including those that will not hire personal care aides. (6) Branch offices use the parent's policies. Adding a new home health care service later requires the full application again, with policies for the new service. (7) At renewal, submit any policies that changed substantively, including those on complaint handling and client evaluation and assessment (COMAR 10.07.05.04I(3)). (8) Limits of this result: the grid is built around home health care services, so a non-medical RSA may request waivers for items such as drug administration and enteral/parenteral nutrition. The application does not list COMAR's other chapter requirements, such as the complaint process (.09), screening (.10) and training (.11), as grid items, and I did not fetch those sections. I also did not review the Medicaid program rules (COMAR 10.09.84 and 10.09.20) for additional written-policy requirements.
